You orchestrate Release 2 slice #111 ("R2 10: Bilingual Template and German redaction") in chrisdoc/surveybeat-next. You are the Opus orchestrator; THIS TASK EXPLICITLY ASKS YOU TO USE SUBAGENTS: `scoper` (model "haiku"), `implementer` (model "haiku") writes all code, `reviewer` (model "sonnet") reviews each implementer diff. Follow ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: scope → you write the plan and small, exact, file-owned briefs → implementer → reviewer → you check the diff and run the full suite.

Read first: `gh issue view 111`, docs/adr/0018-german-localization.md, docs/adr/0009-comments-redacted-at-store-time.md, AGENTS.md, GLOSSARY.md. German landed in PR #113: `Locale` domain module, `de.ts` catalogs, Person/Organization language, `session.locale` in the app. Template lives in packages/domain/src/pulses/Template.ts ("Template's text in code never changes a Pulse"); redaction in the domain `redact` function (find it; table + property tests exist).

Decisions (don't relitigate): the weekly team health Template carries its Questions, labels, and choice options in English and German; a new Pulse copies them in the Lead's language (from the creating Person's resolved locale); existing Pulses are unchanged; Template keys stay the same. German wording: informal "du", product nouns per ADR 0018 (Pulse and Team stay English; Runde, Teamleitung). Draft German Question texts yourself, natural and neutral (they are survey questions — keep the scales' meaning identical), and note in the PR that the product owner reviews them. Redaction recognises German phone formats (+49 / 0049 / leading 0 prefixes; spaces, slashes, dashes, parentheses; mobile 015x/016x/017x and landline area codes) with table tests, without regressing existing cases or over-matching dates/years/plain numbers (add negative cases such as "12.11.2026", "2026", "Raum 3/12").

Workflow: branch `r2-111-template-de` from origin/main. Validation: pnpm typecheck, pnpm typecheck:effect, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test, pnpm test:privacy, pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build. Commit (subject "R2 10: Bilingual Template and German redaction", end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"), push (retry once if rejected without reason), PR with "Closes #111. Part of #101.", summary, verification, a note that German Question wording awaits the product owner's review, body ending "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)" (restore attribution if the shipper drops it). Wait for checks (`gh pr checks <n> --watch`), fix failures, squash-merge your own PR (user-authorized): `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`. Others work in parallel (#103, #105, #108); rebase on conflicts keeping both sides; force-push only your branch.

Final report (≤ 10 lines): what was built, deviations, reviewer findings and handling, test counts, PR URL, merge SHA.

Slice 10 of [Release 2: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/101).

## Goal
German Teams get German Questions, and redaction handles German contact details.

## Acceptance criteria
- The weekly team health Template carries its Questions, labels, and options in English and German; a new Pulse copies them in the Lead's language; existing Pulses are unchanged.
- Redaction (ADR 0009) recognises German phone formats (+49, 0 prefixes, spaces, slashes, dashes) with table tests.

## Tests
- Domain tests for the Template copy and redaction cases.

## Follows
ADR 0018, ADR 0009

## Context

Planned on the [Wayfinder map](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/85). Use `GLOSSARY.md` terms throughout. ADRs are in `docs/adr/`; research in `docs/research/`.

# German ships as typed catalogs per locale, a prerendered answer page per locale, and a bilingual Template

Release 2 adds German to the app, the answer page, and emails ([research](../research/german-localization.md)).

- **Catalogs:** each catalog gets a `de.ts` beside the English one, typed so a missing key, an extra key, or a wrong `{placeholder}` fails typecheck. The message functions take the locale instead of the fixed `"en"`; plurals, dates, and numbers come from `Intl` for that locale.
- **Which language:** a Person's own setting, then the browser's languages, then the Organization's default. Emails render in the language stored with the send when it is created.
- **Answer page:** one prerendered page per locale (`/a`, `/de/a`), each loading only its own answer catalog. The Invitation link picks the page from the recipient's language. ADR 0008's budget applies to each page separately.
- **Words:** informal "du". Pulse and Team stay English; Round → Runde, Lead → Teamleitung, Organization → Organisation, Submission → Einsendung. Claude drafts, the product owner reviews in the PR.
- **Template:** the weekly team health Template ships in both languages; a new Pulse copies its Questions in the Lead's language. Existing Pulses keep their Questions.
- **Privacy:** the language is never stored with a Submission or an Answer. In a small Team it could single out the one German reader.

## Consequences

- The budget test runs per answer page.
- Pages rendered in `MainWorker.ts` (delivery time, unsubscribe) hold hard-coded English and must move to the catalog.
- Redaction gains German phone number cases.
- A Team with mixed languages sees the Pulse's Questions in the language they were created in.
